title: Training Note — Raising the Upgrade Labor Discount on a Plan's Ticket and Alarm History
content:
# Training Note — Raising the Upgrade Labor Discount on a Plan's Ticket and Alarm History

**When is the tier's upgrade labor discount raised?** Where the twelve months to the handling day carry three or more support tickets closed on a plan under the Building Automation Service Plans and at least one monitored alarm the records show with no acknowledgement, the tier's upgrade labor discount is raised by fifteen points. Where the twelve months to the handling day carry three or more support tickets closed on the plan and no monitored alarm the records show with no acknowledgement, the tier's upgrade labor discount is raised by seven points. In every other case the tier's upgrade labor discount stands as the tier carries it.

| Support tickets closed on the plan in the twelve months | Monitored alarms with no acknowledgement in those twelve months | Discount applied to the priced hours |
|---|---|---|
| 3 or more | at least 1 | the tier's upgrade labor discount raised by 15 points |
| 3 or more | none | the tier's upgrade labor discount raised by 7 points |
| fewer than 3 | any number | the tier's upgrade labor discount |

**Which tickets are counted?** Every support ticket closed on the plan in the twelve months to the handling day, however it was closed.

**Which alarms are counted?** Every monitored alarm the records show with no acknowledgement in those twelve months, whatever its class.

**Worked figure (hypothetical).** A plan at a tier whose upgrade labor discount is 20 percent, showing 5 support tickets closed in the twelve months and 2 alarms with no acknowledgement, carries a discount of 35 percent on the priced hours. With no unacknowledged alarm, it carries 27 percent. With 2 tickets closed, it carries the tier's 20 percent.
